top_signal.title: Canadian Small Business Help!
top_signal.summary: Canadian small business owners, I need some guidance because the financial side of running a business is officially out of my depth 😂   For those of you who started as sole proprietors, at roughly what revenue/profit level did you decide it was time to incorporate? Was there a specific dollar amount where your accountant told you it made sense, or were there other factors that pushed you to do it?   My business has grown quite a bit faster than I expected, and now I’m realizing I don’t really know what I should be doing financially as it continues to grow.   I use QuickBooks and I enter my transactions and reconcile everything, and I have a meeting booked with a bookkeeper to help me get my books properly cleaned up. But I constantly feel like something doesn’t look quite right in QuickBooks, and I’m realizing bookkeeping is only one piece of what I’m confused about.   I’m registered for GST/HST and know I need to be setting that money aside, but then there’s personal income tax, figuring out how much I should actually be putting aside, planning for tax time, business expenses, incorporation, and eventually figuring out how to properly pay myself. I’d really like to start paying myself consistently next year if the business can support it.   Basically, I know how to run my actual business. The financial infrastructure behind running a business? I have approximately 700 questions.   Is a CPA the person I should be talking to about all of this? And if so, should I specifically
